items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: How do you think Chalky Banana learned how to play trumpet by following behind Rene's band. And I was playing with Rene

ctx.x: Different fellas, you know, from different bands, you know, where I was playing. I had guitar players playing at different bands, you know. Go around just like a whole lot. That's where Chalky Banana learned how to play trumpet. How do you think Chalky Banana learned how to play trumpet by following behind Rene's band. And I was playing with Rene and Chalky didn't know nothing about trumpet. But he used to, he got good with Rene and he'd buy, he know Rene drank wine. He'd get a half a gallon of wine, you see. And…
What did you call the guys that would steal? Nothing, nothing.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: I played, when I was playing, I was, when I played with Rene, that's practically most every, every dance he played for outside, dances he had to advertise.

ctx.x: I wonder about that. What bands did you play with when you'd be advertising?

Well, it's like I said, I played, when I was playing, I was, when I played with Rene, that's practically most every, every dance he played for outside, dances he had to advertise. People hire, when they hire a band, they hire for the advertising, too, you see. They give you two dollars extra for that advertising. Did Rene ever buck against Louis Armstrong? Oh, Armstrong, practically yes. Well, Armstrong, he didn't, he didn't, didn't much, he didn't do much advertising. Uh-huh. You know, because when Armstrong…

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: him and Rene had to run in again then he come back and got me again. And I went back and stayed with him.

ctx.x: He got a little jazz from Rene. Yeah. That's where he got it from. And I was telling Mr. Russell, you remember after Rene was kind of going down. I had to play this jippie dance. His wife. She live in Rapshap. Yeah. She calls me and says take Henry to learn the music without checking. Yeah. When him and son used to come over. Yeah son Thomas. Yeah. Fan joke there. Uh huh. And I start him off that he could read his reviews. Yeah. That's right. That's right. And the same time then Joe got interested. He never could…

I remember Joe started with the clarinet for that. Because he had no son and Rene and it was strange. Yeah. Yeah. And uh uh the old man Rene uh uh Guernie was playing bass with him first. See. Mmhmm. With Rene. He started with Rene. After that he they had a fallen out and then that's where they take me. And uh after I had broke up with him then they take him to Chester. Is that Chester's artist? Chester's artist. They took him on the bass and they had uh him and Rene had to run in again then he come back and got…

Well you know Rene had taken Simon too. Yeah. Simon Moreira. When you had a Bitskin band came in. Huh? When you had a Bitskin band came in. What band? Bitskin. Yeah. You know a Zuta band you call it. Oh you're talking about uh. You're talking about uh.
I'll ask a couple questions, see like where you were born right here in New Orleans.

I started the playing in 1904 at Hugh Cloth's Dance Hall with O'Neill Lavish's Band, Franklin Y. Iberville. 1905 at Tom Anderson with Moran's Band, Basin and Iberville. 1907 at Harry Parker's Dance Hall, Dawson and Minetta's Band, Franklin between Iberville and Benwood. 1910 at Biller Phillips Dance Hall, Cornelius Jackson's Band, Franklin near Iberville. 1912 Liberty near Iberville, Huntson Nagel's Dance Hall with Joe Oliver's Band. 1915 with Chris Kelly's Band. 1918 Kid René's Band. 1921 Pippa Light Charles Band.
